kai: heads up — noticed a regression on Mistral-8x7B when using sliding-window attention + aggressive batching heuristics. p99 latency up ~12% after the recent kernel-selector change. :eyes:

maya: ah — which kernel change? the scanline->tile handoff from yesterday?

kai: yep. looks like when `rope_scale` != 1.0 and windowing is enabled the kernel picker prefers tile kernels that blow out tail latency on short sequences. quick paste of perf run: 

```
model: mistral-8x7b
seq: 256 (sliding window)
batch: 8 -> adaptive batching on
rope_scale: 0.98
kernel_switches: tile: 78, scanline: 12
latency_ms: p50=18.2 p95=45.4 p99=82.1 (before patch p99=73.1)
kv_cache_hits: 86% -> 68%
```

oliver: kv_cache_hits drop is suspicious. are we losing prefix cache alignment when rope_scale != 1.0?

jess: maybe rope scaling shifts token positions enough that our prefix fingerprinting misses and we fall back to cold-path kernel with full recompute?

kai: that was my hunch. I bisected: revert kernel-selector commit f2d9 -> p99 back to 74ms. So selector is the likely culprit, but only reproduces when sliding-window + non-1 rope_scale + batch fusion enabled.

sam: can you share the minimal repro? I can run on a dev box.

kai: repro command: 

```bash
./serve_local --model=mistral-8x7b --seq=4096 --sliding-window=256 --rope-scale=0.98 --batcher.window_target=8 --batcher.max_fuse=3 --kernel-picker=auto
```

oliver: thanks. i'll run with `--kernel-picker=scanline-only` and compare kernel timings.

ci-bot: canary-deploy kickoff: infra/canary/2175004321 by kai (reason: perf regression triage) :rocket:

jess: quick profiling snippet i ran: 

```
# per-token timeline (simplified)
token 0..128: scanline kernel, avg 1.9ms/token
token 129..256: tile kernel, avg 3.5ms/token (KV lookups increased)
kv_lookup_waits: 4.2ms extra on tile path
```

nate: does the tile kernel do more global memory ops that interact badly with our KV layout when pos indices shift? might be a memory-alignment/regression.

kai: exactly — hypothesis: rope_scale changes effective floating-point pos enc calc, leading to different chunking of keys (tile boundaries). tile kernel uses a tiled KV layout which mis-aligns and triggers extra mem copies. scanline path avoids the copies.

maya: solution space: 1) force scanline for sliding-window when rope_scale != 1.0 2) change fingerprinting to be rope-scale aware 3) adjust tile kernel to handle shifted boundaries without copies

jess: i prefer (2) as long-term: make prefix-key hashing use quantized pos after applying rope_scale, so we keep cache hits stable across small scale perturbations. low-risk patch.

sam: (1) is fastest to roll — feature-flag a conservative selector: if sliding-window && abs(rope_scale - 1.0) > 0.01 -> prefer scanline.

kai: i'll open a PR for the selector revert/flag and a short test harness. can we attach a small unit test that simulates altered rope_scale and asserts kv_cache_hit rate > 80%?

oliver: add perf CI job: run a short sliding-window workload pre/post and assert p99 delta < 5%. we should gate the kernel-selector change.

ci-bot: PR opened: r/infra#6421 by kai — "selector: guard tile handoff for sliding-window + rope_scale"

jess: also noticed an attention-mask quirk: when sliding window overlaps are not multiples of tile width, tile kernel will mask across boundary differently (off-by-one) and we end up with extra prefix recompute. small mask normalization fix should help.

nate: good catch — that's the "mask shadow" I mentioned in yesterday's notes. can we add a test for mask-normalization alignment?

kai: plan: (A) quick revert/flag to restore perf (B) add rope-aware fingerprinting ticket (C) tile kernel mask align fix (D) perf CI gating. i'll take A and C, jess will lead B, oliver will add CI job.

maya: timeline?

kai: i'll get the revert patch + unit test in today, canary for tomorrow morning. if canary looks good we'll merge fully.

sam: i'll standby to run regression harness across Mistral-7B too — must ensure 7B doesn't regress when selector flips.

jess: note: Mistral-7B has different head/kv dims so tile path might behave differently — keep both models in perf CI.

oliver: thumbs up. post canary logs here once done and include `nvprof` kernel timeline. :thumbsup:

kai: thanks all — dropping initial perf logs into the issue. will update thread after canary. :rocket:
